chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Who Issa El Saieh was
summary: Budd describes El Saieh's Arab and Lebanese family background, the family business and his art dealing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Budd, I'd just like to mention here right now, for the record's sake, that (Esa Sayeehee) was a white Haitian.

His father was Arabic. And his mother was from Bethlehem. So she was Lebanese, and she was born -- she told me when I was down there -- her house was right across from the manger where Jesus Christ was born, and of course they have a place where they have a business called the Haitian and American Development Corporation, and they import all of the dry goods into that country, and El-Sahee was into construction. He -- through their corporation they could order anything from the United States. They had permanent citizenship here, and they were a millionaire family.
I remember I met him through you.
Now he's great art dealer. He deals in primitive art of Haiti, and he travels all over the world, and he's into it. He's probably a millionaire in his own right now.
